Baccarat Side Bets Explained: Dragon Bonus, Panda 8, and Why Their House Edge Runs So Much Higher

Published September 21, 2026 · 9 min read · By the OddsLighthouse Editorial Team

Sit down at a baccarat table and the felt in front of you usually has more betting spots than just Banker, Player, and Tie. Small boxes labeled Dragon Bonus, Panda 8, or Perfect Pairs sit off to the side, tempting with payouts as high as 25-to-1 or 30-to-1 on a single hand. Those side bets are real, legal, and available at plenty of casinos and online tables — but they're also where baccarat's famously tight house edge quietly disappears. The base game is one of the best mathematical bets on the entire casino floor. The side bets built around it usually aren't.

Why side bets exist next to a game this tight

The base Banker bet in baccarat runs a house edge of roughly 1.06%, and Player sits around 1.24% — numbers competitive with blackjack and craps odds bets, among the lowest on the floor. That tightness is exactly why side bets exist. A casino earning barely more than a penny on the dollar from the main game has every incentive to offer alternative wagers on the same cards that carry a much fatter margin, packaged as an exciting, high-payout option sitting right next to a bet most players already understand. Nothing about a side bet changes how the hand is dealt or resolved for Banker, Player, or Tie — it's a separate wager layered on top, settled by outcomes the base game already produces.

Dragon Bonus: betting on the margin, not just the winner

Dragon Bonus is a margin bet: you're not just picking Banker or Player to win, you're betting on how convincingly they win. A "natural" win — an 8 or 9 on the first two cards — typically pays even money on either side. Beyond that, payouts scale with the winning margin once a hand goes to a third card: win by 4 runs and it might pay 1-to-1, win by 8 or more and payouts can climb into the 10-to-1 to 30-to-1 range depending on the house's paytable. A push (win by less than 4) simply returns the stake.

Winning marginTypical Dragon Bonus payout
Natural win (8 or 9)1 to 1
Win by 41 to 1
Win by 52 to 1
Win by 64 to 1
Win by 76 to 1
Win by 810 to 1
Win by 9 (non-natural)30 to 1

Because a blowout margin in baccarat is genuinely rare — most hands are decided by small gaps — Dragon Bonus carries a noticeably asymmetric edge depending on which side you back. Betting the Dragon on Banker generally runs a house edge in the neighborhood of 2.5% to 3%, while betting it on Player is considerably worse, often north of 7%, because Banker's structural third-card drawing rules make big Banker margins somewhat more common than big Player margins.

Why this matters: two versions of the "same" side bet — Dragon on Banker versus Dragon on Player — can carry more than double the house edge difference from one another, even though they look like a symmetrical choice on the layout.

Panda 8: a rare three-card Banker total

Panda 8 pays out when the Banker hand wins with a three-card total of 8. Because it requires both a specific total and a specific number of cards drawn — a natural 8 on the first two cards doesn't count — it's a genuinely uncommon outcome, and the payout reflects that scarcity, commonly listed around 25-to-1. The tradeoff is a house edge that typically runs in the 10% to 12% range, well outside what most bettors would accept if the number were stated plainly instead of buried under a big, flashy payout figure.

Perfect Pairs: betting on the first two cards

Perfect Pairs bets resolve before the hand even finishes developing — it's a wager that either the Banker's or Player's first two cards form a pair (or, in some versions, that either hand does). Some tables split this into tiers: any pair pays a lower amount, a suited pair (same rank and suit) pays considerably more. Typical payouts run from around 5-to-1 for any pair up to 25-to-1 or higher for a perfect suited pair, with a blended house edge commonly cited in the 9% to 11% range depending on the specific paytable and pair-type rules a given casino uses.

Lucky 6: the EZ Baccarat companion bet

Lucky 6 shows up specifically alongside EZ Baccarat, a popular commission-free variant where the standard 5% commission on winning Banker bets is replaced by a single rule: a Banker win on a three-card total of 7 pushes instead of paying (this is sometimes called the "Dragon 7" push). Lucky 6 is the companion side bet in that format — it pays when Banker wins with a total of 6, typically around 12-to-1 for a three-card 6 and a higher 20-to-1 for a two-card 6. Because commission-free Banker already shifts some of the house's usual take into that Dragon 7 push rule, Lucky 6 tends to carry a notably steep house edge of its own, often cited well into the double digits and sometimes above 15% depending on the exact paytable a casino runs.

House edge, side by side

Laid out together, the gap between the base game and its side bets is stark:

BetApproximate house edge
Banker (base game)~1.06%
Player (base game)~1.24%
Tie (base game)~14.4%
Dragon Bonus — Banker side~2.5%–3%
Dragon Bonus — Player side~7%–8%
Panda 8~10%–12%
Perfect Pairs~9%–11%
Lucky 6 (EZ Baccarat)~13%–17%+

The base Tie bet already has a reputation as baccarat's weakest wager, and it's worth noticing that most of these side bets run an edge comparable to or worse than Tie — they're simply marketed with more exciting payout numbers and less familiarity, so fewer players have an intuitive sense of how bad the math actually is.

Why casinos push these bets so visibly

Side bets solve a real business problem for the casino: a game where the house edge is under 1.5% on both main outcomes doesn't generate much margin per hand compared to games like slots or Tie itself. Side bets sit right on the same layout, require no extra dealing time, and let a casino meaningfully raise its average take per hand from players who add even a small side wager on top of their main bet. The high advertised payouts aren't dishonest — Dragon Bonus really can pay 30-to-1 — but a big number attached to a rare event is a classic way to make a high house edge feel like an exciting opportunity rather than what it actually is: a significantly worse long-run bet than the game sitting right next to it.

Common mistakes

  • Assuming all side bets carry a similar edge. They don't — Dragon Bonus on Banker and Lucky 6 can differ by 10 percentage points or more, even though both feel like a minor add-on to the main hand.
  • Chasing a side bet after a near-miss. A three-card 7 falling one short of a Panda 8, or a pair that almost hit, doesn't change the odds on the next hand — every hand is independent, and side bets reshuffle the same steep math every time.
  • Sizing a side bet the same as the main wager. Given the edge gap, a side bet sized like a primary Banker or Player bet puts a disproportionate share of total risk into the weakest bet on the table.

None of this means side bets are off-limits — plenty of players enjoy them specifically for the bigger, rarer payouts, and that's a legitimate reason to play a game for entertainment. The distinction worth keeping straight is that Dragon Bonus, Panda 8, Perfect Pairs, and Lucky 6 are a different kind of bet from Banker and Player, not a minor variation on them. For the fundamentals these side bets build on top of, see our baccarat basics guide, and for how house edge is calculated generally, see our guide on how house edge works.

Frequently asked questions

Are baccarat side bets rigged or unfair?

No — they're legitimate, published bets available at licensed casinos, with payouts that match their stated odds. They're simply structured with a much higher house edge than the main Banker or Player bets, which is disclosed in the paytable even if it isn't emphasized.

Which baccarat side bet has the lowest house edge?

Among common side bets, Dragon Bonus on the Banker side tends to run the lowest edge, typically in the 2.5%–3% range, though it's still meaningfully higher than the base Banker or Player bets it sits alongside.

Do side bets affect how the main Banker/Player/Tie hand plays out?

No. Side bets are wagered and settled separately from the base game. The cards are dealt and the third-card drawing rules apply exactly the same whether or not anyone at the table has placed a side bet.

Why does Lucky 6 specifically appear in EZ Baccarat?

EZ Baccarat removes the standard 5% commission on winning Banker bets and replaces it with a push on Banker wins by a three-card 7. Lucky 6 is offered as a companion side bet in that same no-commission format, giving players a way to bet specifically on Banker winning with a 6.
